resources.description: Common SQL patterns and optimization techniques.

items.ex: SELECT * FROM products ORDER BY price DESC;
SELECT * FROM orders INNER JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.id;

items.desc: All from left, matching from right
items.ex: SELECT * FROM users LEFT JOIN orders ON users.id = orders.user_id;

items.desc: All from right, matching from left
items.ex: SELECT * FROM products RIGHT JOIN inventory ON products.id = inventory.product_id;

items.desc: All records when there's a match
items.ex: SELECT * FROM table1 FULL JOIN table2 ON table1.id = table2.id;
SELECT * FROM colors CROSS JOIN sizes;
SELECT department, AVG(salary) FROM employees GROUP BY department;
SELECT department, AVG(salary) FROM employees GROUP BY department HAVING AVG(salary) > 50000;
UPDATE users SET status = 'active' WHERE last_login > '2023-01-01';
DELETE FROM sessions WHERE expires_at < NOW();
MERGE INTO target USING source ON target.id = source.id WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET value = source.value WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (id, value) VALUES (source.id, source.value);
WITH top_earners AS (SELECT * FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 10) SELECT * FROM top_earners;
SELECT name, salary, AVG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department) as avg_dept_salary FROM employees;
SELECT name FROM customers UNION SELECT name FROM employees;
SELECT name FROM products WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM inventory WHERE products.id = inventory.product_id AND quantity > 0);
SELECT name, CASE WHEN age < 18 THEN 'minor' WHEN age < 65 THEN 'adult' ELSE 'senior' END FROM users;
